**It is read strictly:** a field this build does not know, in the entry
or in its command, refuses the request
(`docs/decisions/0028-enforced-values-fail-closed.md`). An entry the
user writes is accepted from the moment it is written, and a command
among them becomes an allow rule once the project is trusted: a field
that is not understood could be the one that narrows it, such as an
expiry. Its `check` is read as every check is: it is stored and shown,
and whatever runs checks puts each one to the permission engine.

check.description: A test that shows it still holds.

anyOf.description: A request failed and will be tried again.
A compaction started, finished or failed.
A configured limit was reached or is near.
Something about the sandbox.
Instruction files changed.
A request ran at a different speed from the one asked for.
A speed tier's cooldown began or ended.
Anything else.
The project's checks: a round starting or ended, or checks offered (since step 19).
A variant this version of the protocol does not know. Receivers skip it or show it generically.

Notice.description: Something transient that front ends should show. It is never sent to the model and is not an item.  Every notice has a `message` in words, so a client can show a kind of notice it does not know.

NoticeItem.description:
A message the harness added to the conversation. The model sees it.

This is not the `notice` event ([`Notice`](crate::event::Notice)), which
tells front ends about something transient and is never sent to the model.

anyOf.description: Instruction files changed.
The user edited the plan.
The same call keeps repeating without effect.
The project's checks failed.
A limit was reached.
Something else the model needs to know.
The repository map: an epoch's view of the workspace, given once in it.
The project profile changed since the model was given it (since step 17).
A value this version of the protocol does not know. Receivers need a default branch.

NoticeSource.description: Why the harness added a notice to the conversation.

Origin.description:
What produced an assistant message. Raw blocks are valid only for replay
to the same protocol, and to a model that can read them.

account_scope.description:
The account or organisation the credential belonged to, where the
provider ties opaque reasoning to it. Never the credential.

anyOf.description: Text.
An image.
A tool call by the model.
The result of a tool call.
Reasoning by the model.
A provider block with no neutral form.
A variant this version of the protocol does not know. Receivers skip it or show it generically.

PathSet.description: A set of paths: everything, or the trees under some roots.

all.description: Every path. When set, `roots` is ignored.

roots.description: The roots of the trees in the set.

PeerInfo.description: The name and version of one side of a connection.

PermissionDenial.description:
A tool call that was refused because nothing could approve it: the
usual reason a headless run does less than was expected.

turn_id.description: The turn the call belonged to.

approvals.description: The approvals in force for the session.

Plan.description:
The plan for the current work: a task list that the agent keeps and the
user can see and change.

revision.description:
Goes up by one with every change, so a client can tell which of two
plans is newer.

after.description: The item it goes after. Absent: at the end.

anyOf.description: Put the items in a new order.
Mark an item as skipped.
Put a skipped item back to be done. Added in step 24.
Replace an item's text.
Add an item.
Remove an item.
A variant this version of the protocol does not know. Receivers skip it or show it generically.

PlanEdit.description: One edit a user makes to the plan. It takes effect at once, and reaches the model as a notice at the next safe boundary.

id.description: The task's id, stable across edits.

PlanItemRef.description: Names one plan item: the payload of `skip` and `remove`.

PlanReorder.description: Puts the plan's items in a new order.

order.description: Every item's id, in the new order.

PlanResult.description: A result that is the plan.

anyOf.description: Not started.
Being worked on.
Finished.
Left out, by the agent or by the user.
A value this version of the protocol does not know. Receivers need a default branch.

PriceTier.description: The prices of a request whose input is larger than a threshold.

above_input_tokens.description: The tier applies when the request's input tokens exceed this.

Prices.description:
One rate card: what a million tokens of each class cost. Every price is a
whole number of nano-dollars (1e-9 US dollars) per million tokens, so
`4_000_000_000` is $4.00 per million.

cache_read.description: Input tokens read from the cache. Absent when the model has no cache price.

cache_write.description: Input tokens written to the cache, per lifetime class.

input.description: Input tokens that were not read from or written to the cache.

tiers.description:
Rate cards that replace this one for larger requests, by ascending
threshold. The last tier whose threshold the request passes applies.

ProjectDetectParams.description:
`project/detect`: the build, test and check commands a session's project
names in its own files (`Cargo.toml`, `package.json`'s scripts, a
`Makefile`'s targets, `go.mod`, `pyproject.toml`), for the first run's
last step (since step 25). A read, beside the lane, for any client that
has the session open, as `workspace/files` is: the files are read
through the session's path resolver and its read rules, and nothing is
kept, learned or run.

commands.description:
The commands found, by file in the order the files are looked at,
each named once. Only lines of plain words that the command
observer classes as a build, a test run or a check are given.

ProjectEntriesResult.description: A result that is project entries.

entries.description:
The entries: all of them for `project/list`, the changed ones for
`project/update`.

problems.description:
What is wrong with the project's files, each in a sentence: a file
that cannot be read as it is, and what is used in its place. Added
in step 17.

ProjectEntry.description: One entry of the project profile or memory.

accepted_at.description:
When the user accepted it. For a `command` entry this is what puts
it on the project's safe list; an entry that became active by
itself has none. Added in step 17.

basis.description: How the harness came to hold it. Absent for an entry the user wrote.

check.description: A test that shows it still holds.

confirmed_at.description: When it was last seen to hold.

evidence.description: Where it was learned: a path and line, a command, or the user's words.

expires_at.description:
When it stops being used unless confirmed again. Entries the user
wrote do not expire.

observations.description:
For an observed entry: how many times the harness saw it hold.
Added in step 17.

text.description:
The entry in words: the rule, the fact, the test's name, or what the
command is.

ProjectKey.description: The key that names a project in the state directory. Never a path.

ProjectListParams.description:
Names a project by a session of it, or by its workspace root. Exactly one
is set.

add.description:
Entries the user writes, added after the changes. Each is active at
once. Added in step 17.

session_id.description: A session of the project. Exactly one of this and `workspace` is set.

ProjectUpdated.description: Project profile or memory entries were proposed or changed.

entries.description: The entries that are new or changed, as they are now.

ProviderBlockPart.description:
Something the provider produced that the neutral model does not name:
server-side tool use and its results, compaction blocks, fallback markers.

block_type.description: The provider's name for the block type, for display.

ProviderId.description: A provider: an endpoint that speaks a protocol, by its configured name.

ProviderLimits.description:
The limits one provider last reported. A provider that reports none has
no entry, and a front end shows "not available".

available.description:
Whether the account or key may make calls now, where the provider
says. Added in step 16.

balances.description:
Money left, one entry a currency, where the provider's usage
endpoint reports it (the opt-in refresh). Amounts in different
currencies are never added together or converted. Added in step 16.

next_epoch.description:
When the provider's next accounting period begins, where it names
one without saying which limits it resets (Venice.ai's "epoch").
It is not a limit's reset time. Added in step 16.

QuestionRequest.description: `question/ask`: a question for the user, from the agent or an extension.

choices.description: Answers to pick from. Empty: free text.

extension.description: The extension that asks. Absent: the agent.

turn_id.description: The turn, when the question belongs to one.

answer.description: The answer. Absent: the user declined to answer.

RawJson.description:
JSON text kept exactly as a provider sent it, carried as a string so
that no parser on the way can reorder keys, change escapes or round
numbers. Replay sends it back unchanged. Clients treat it as opaque.

ReasoningControl.description:
A model's reasoning control. Depth is a per-model set, never a number on a
shared scale.

default.description: For `levels`: the level used when none is set.

kind.description: Which kind of control this is.

levels.description: For `levels`: the model's own level names, from least to most.

max_tokens.description: For `budget`: the largest budget, in tokens.

min_tokens.description: For `budget`: the smallest budget, in tokens.

anyOf.description: The model has no reasoning control.
An ordered set of named effort levels.
A token budget within a range.
A value this version of the protocol does not know. Receivers need a default branch.

ReasoningControlKind.description: How a model's reasoning depth is controlled.

raw.description:
The provider's own block, which holds the opaque payload (a
signature, encrypted content). It is replayed unchanged to a model
that can read it and dropped for any other.

text.description: The visible reasoning or its summary. Often empty.

RefreshOutcome.description: What one provider's usage endpoint answered.

error.description: Why it did not. The figures kept from before stay as they were.

limits.description:
The figures, when the refresh worked. They are also kept, and
`usage/report` shows them from then on.

RequestId.description: The id that ties a response to its request: a number or a string, chosen by the side that sends the request.

RequestResolved.description:
A request from the server (an approval, a question, a trust prompt) was
settled without this client. The client withdraws its prompt.

request_id.description: The JSON-RPC id of the request, as this client received it.

RequestUsage.description:
The usage of one request to a model: what was used, at which speed, and
what it cost.

billing.description: How the usage is paid for.

catalog_version.description: The version of the catalog whose prices were used.

cost.description:
The cost, fixed when the request was recorded. Absent when the model
has no known price.

role.description: The role the request was made in.

speed.description:
The speed the request **ran at**: the provider's own report where it
gives one, otherwise the speed that was sent. The cost is priced at
this speed's rate.

speed_requested.description: The speed that was asked for, when the request ran at another one.

time_to_first_token_ms.description: Milliseconds from sending the request to the first token.

anyOf.description: Another client answered it.
Nobody answered in time, and the default was applied.
The turn was interrupted before anybody answered.
A value this version of the protocol does not know. Receivers need a default branch.

Resolution.description: How a request from the server to its clients was settled.

RetryNotice.description: Notice: a request failed and will be tried again.

attempt.description: Which attempt comes next, counting from 1.

max_attempts.description: The most attempts a request gets.

RewindFile.description: One file of a rewind's plan.

path.description:
The file as the session's checkpoints name it: relative to the
workspace's root, or absolute outside it.

status.description: Whether it can be put back now.

to.description: What it would go back to.

why_not.description: Why it cannot be put back, when `status` is `cannot`.

anyOf.description: It is as the harness left it: putting it back is safe.
It is already as it would be put back.
It was changed after the harness left it: the rewind asks before it puts it back, and keeps it unless told otherwise.
It cannot be put back, and is left as it is: `why_not` says why.
A value this version of the protocol does not know. Receivers need a default branch.

RewindFileStatus.description: Whether a file of a rewind's plan can be put back now.

anyOf.description: Its content before the turns undone.
No file: it did not exist then, and would be removed.
Not known: a command changed it, and what it held before was not recorded. It is never removed or overwritten.
A value this version of the protocol does not know. Receivers need a default branch.

RewindTarget.description: What a rewind would put a file back to.

anyOf.description: What it held before is not known.
Its earlier content was too large to keep.
Its earlier content is no longer in the session's store.
A checkpoint of the turns undone cannot be read.
A directory on its way, or the file itself, is now a link.
A value this version of the protocol does not know. Receivers need a default branch.

RewindWhyNot.description: Why a file of a rewind's plan cannot be put back.

anyOf.description: The user, or the harness speaking for the user.
The model.
The results of the tool calls in the assistant message before it, in call order.
A value this version of the protocol does not know. Receivers need a default branch.

RoleSettings.description:
A change to the settings of one model role. A field that is absent is
left as it is.

effort.description:
The reasoning level: one of the model's own levels, or a portable
alias (`minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `max`).

provider.description:
The provider that serves the model. Needed only when two providers
have a model with the same id.

speed.description:
The speed for this role. For `main` it overrides the session's
speed. The utility roles (`fast`, `judge`) do not follow the session's
speed: they run at `standard` unless this is set.

RoleState.description: What one model role of a session is set to, and what is in effect.

effort.description: The reasoning level as it was set.

effort_in_effect.description: The model's own level that the setting maps to.

speed.description:
The speed this role is set to: its own setting; without one, the
session's speed for `main` and `standard` for a utility role.
Required, so that a reader never has to guess a default.

speed_cooldown_until.description: When a cooldown of `speed` ends, while one is running.

speed_in_effect.description:
The speed its next request will ask for. It differs from `speed`
when the model does not offer that speed, or while the speed is in a
cooldown. Required.

Rule.description: A permission rule. `deny` beats `ask` beats `allow`, whatever the order.

effect.description: The effect the rule is about. An effect that is not listed is refused.

match.description:
What it matches: a path glob, a command pattern, a host, or a
`server/tool` name.

anyOf.description: The effect may happen without asking.
The supervisor is asked.
The effect is refused.

SandboxNotice.description:
Notice: something about the sandbox the user should know: it is not
enforcing, a command ran outside it, a protected path changed.

SandboxPolicy.description: What a child process may touch, whatever it runs.

network.description: Whether the network may be used.

protect.description: Paths inside `write` that must not be changed.

anyOf.description: It does. Levels above `supervised` are available.
It does not: the OS has no backend yet, or the kernel lacks what the backend needs. Commands that run are not confined.
A value this version of the protocol does not know. Receivers need a default branch.

SandboxStatus.description: Whether the OS sandbox confines child processes on this machine.

experimental.description:
The experimental features it turned on for this connection: the ones
the client asked for that it has.

mcp.description: It was built with the MCP client.

SessionArtifactParams.description:
`session/artifact`: a stored artifact of a session, such as the whole
output of a check. Added in step 24.

cut.description: Whether `text` holds less than all of it.

text.description:
Its text, as stored, up to the server's limit. Not UTF-8 where it is
stored is replaced with `U+FFFD`.

SessionCompactParams.description:
`session/compact`: an idle session compacts in a turn of its own that
sends nothing else; a running one at its next safe boundary. A turn
whose last request is under way has none left: when it ends, the turn
that follows takes the compaction at its first boundary, and when none
follows, a turn that only compacts runs. An interrupt drops it.

focus.description: What the summary should keep in particular.

seq.description: Goes up by one per event per session. A gap means events were missed.

SessionEvent.description: An event with its envelope: which session, where in its sequence, and which turn. The event's own fields sit beside the envelope's.

SessionForkParams.description:
`session/fork`. Names where the new session ends by at most one of
`at` and `before`; with neither it keeps all of the session. Both are
refused (`invalid_params`).

at.description: The last item the new session keeps.

before.description:
The item the new session ends just before (since step 25): it keeps
what the session's log holds before that item's entry, and nothing
of the item or after it. The id of a prompt that began a turn forks
from before the turn's first entry: what the turn recorded before
its prompt (the notices that waited for it, the epoch's map) is left
out with it, and whatever the log holds between the turn before and
the turn (that turn's last checkpoint, a plan the person edited) is
kept. A core from before step 25 ignores it, and forks all of the
session: its result's `before` is then absent.

SessionForkResult.description:
The result of `session/fork`: the new session's state, and where it
ends when it was asked to end before an item (since the review of the
fixes of step 25's second pull request).

before.description:
The `before` of the request, given back when the new session ends
just before that item. A client that asked for `before` takes a
result without it for a fork of all of the session: a core that
does not know the field ignores it, and forks all of the session,
as `session/read`'s `redacted` is given back for the same reason.

SessionIdle.description: The session has no running turn and no queued prompt.

cursor.description: Where to continue: the `next_cursor` of the page before.

workspace.description: Only sessions of this workspace. Absent: every workspace.

SessionListResult.description:
The result of `session/list`: the session added to last first (by
`updated_at`, the id breaking a tie), not the one made last.

config.description:
Configuration overrides for this session, as the configuration file
would have them. They rank as command-line flags do.

cwd.description:
Where the session's commands start when they name no directory: an
absolute path inside `workspace` (the directory the person started
the harness in, below the root it found). Absent: the root. Kept in
the session's log, so that a resumed session starts there too (since
the follow-ups of step 23).

ephemeral.description: Whether to keep the session in memory only, with no log.

settings.description: The settings to start with. Anything absent comes from configuration.

workspace.description: The workspace root: an absolute path on the server's machine.

cursor.description: Where to continue: the `next_cursor` of the page before.

item_id.description:
Read only this item. An item in progress comes back with the content
it has so far.

redacted.description:
For an export (since step 25): every item's text masked by the
core's own secret filter, as the session log's writer masks it, the
provider's blocks (`raw`) left out, and the items still in progress
left out (named in `incomplete`). A session kept only in memory is
masked the same. The result says it was masked (its `redacted`).

SessionReadResult.description: The result of `session/read`: items of the active branch, oldest first.

incomplete.description: The ones among them that are still in progress.

masked.description:
With `redacted`: how many values are masked in `items`, by the log
as it was written or as they were read (since step 25).

redacted.description:
The items were masked for an export, as `redacted` asked (since
step 25). A client that asked for `redacted` writes nothing without
it: a server that does not know the field reads the items unmasked,
and its result reads `false` here.

seq.description:
The `seq` of the last event sent for the session when the items were
read. Events after it are not in this result.

SessionRef.description: Names a session: the parameters of every method that takes nothing else.

SessionResult.description: A result that is the session's state.

SessionRewindParams.description:
`session/rewind`: moves the active branch back to an item, or to just
before one, putting files back if asked. The point is named by exactly
one of `to` and `before`: both, or neither, are refused
(`invalid_params`).

**It may ask a question** (since step 23). With `restore_files`, a file
edited since the harness left it is put back only if the person says so:
the session's `user` clients that answer questions are put one
`question/ask` naming those files, with the choices "Put them back" and
"Keep them as they are". No client to ask, no answer, a client that goes
away, the session's close and the core's end all keep the files. The
result comes once the question is settled; a session closed meanwhile is
not moved back (`session_not_open`).

before.description:
The item of the active branch to go back to just before (since step
25): the active position becomes the entry the item's own follows,
and everything from the item on is undone, nothing before it. The id
of a prompt that began a turn goes back to before the turn's first
entry, where `session/undo` goes back to when that turn is the last:
the turn and every later one are undone, what the turn recorded
before its prompt (the notices that waited for it, the epoch's map)
with them, and what the log holds between the turn before and the
turn (that turn's last checkpoint, a plan the person edited) is kept.
A core from before step 25 refuses a rewind with `before` alone, for
want of `to`.

plan.description:
The `mark` of the plan `session/rewind_plan` gave, which the person
was shown (since step 25). The plan is made again, and the rewind is
refused (`plan_changed`), changing nothing, when it is not that one:
when the point it goes back to, the active position it goes back
from or its turns differ, and with `restore_files` also when what it
would do to any file does. Absent: no plan is checked.

restore_files.description:
Whether to put files back as they were at that point, from the
snapshots of the turns that are undone.

to.description: The last item to keep on the active branch.

SessionRewindPlanParams.description:
`session/rewind_plan`: what `session/rewind` to the same point would do
now, changing nothing (since step 25). A front end shows it before it
asks whether to put files back: the turns it would undo, and each file
they changed with what it would go back to. The point is named as the
rewind names it, by exactly one of `to` and `before`. Refused as
`session/rewind` would be: `invalid_params` for both or neither,
`role_not_allowed` for an observer, `session_not_stored` for a session
with no log, `unknown_item`, `turn_running` while a turn runs, and
`history_changing` while another change of the history is under way (a
rewind's question still open).

before.description:
The item of the active branch the rewind would go back to just
before, as `session/rewind`'s `before`.

to.description: The last item the rewind would keep on the active branch.

SessionRewindPlanResult.description:
The result of `session/rewind_plan`: the plan the core would carry out
(`docs/architecture/07-sessions-and-context.md`, "Snapshots and undo").

files.description: The files those turns changed, by name.

mark.description:
The plan in a few characters: given back as `session/rewind`'s
`plan`, it has that rewind refused when the plan has changed since.
It holds the point the rewind goes back to, the active position it
goes back from, the turns it undoes and what it does to each file.

turns.description: The turns it would undo, wholly or in part, oldest first.

unreadable.description:
A checkpoint of those turns cannot be read: what they changed is not
wholly known, and no file would be put back.

settings.description: What to change. Anything absent stays as it is.

SessionSettings.description:
A change to a session's settings: the parameters of `session/set`, and
the settings a new session starts with. A field that is absent is left as
it is.

level.description: The level (permission mode). Raising it needs the `user` role.

speed.description:
The session's speed: what the `main` role runs at unless it sets
its own. The utility roles do not inherit it.

SessionState.description: A session's metadata and current state.

lease_id.description: The lease in force. `lease/get` returns its terms.

level.description: The level of the lease in force.

parent.description: The session it was forked from.

queue_length.description: How many prompts are queued behind the running turn.

running_turn.description: The turn that is running, if one is.

sandbox.description: Whether the sandbox confines the session's commands.

seq.description:
The `seq` of the last event sent for this session. Events after it
are live.

speed.description:
The session's speed setting: what the `main` role runs at unless it
sets its own. Required.

trust.description:
What the user has said of the project's trust, for a front end's
status (since step 23). It informs only: what trust turns on is the
core's to decide.

workspace.description: The workspace root. An absolute path on the server's machine.

write_roots.description:
The directories the session's commands may write to, as absolute
paths: the workspace, the session's temporary directory and any the
configuration adds. A front end keeps a program it runs for the
person (an external editor) out of them, since a command could have
put one there (since step 23). The list is the same whether or not
commands are confined: where they are not (the sandbox off, the
`unrestricted` level, or a system the sandbox does not confine yet)
a command may write anywhere, and keeping out of these protects
nothing then.

SessionSummary.description: A stored session, in a list.

model.description: The main model it last used.

parent.description: The session it was forked from.

updated_at.description: When it was last added to.

SessionUndoParams.description:
`session/undo`: steps back before the session's last turn, its first
included, and records the step as an undo (since step 23).

**It may ask a question** (since step 23). With `restore_files`, a file
edited since the harness left it is put back only if the person says so:
the session's `user` clients that answer questions are put one
`question/ask` naming those files, with the choices "Put them back" and
"Keep them as they are". No client to ask, no answer, a client that goes
away, the session's close and the core's end all keep the files. The
result comes once the question is settled; a session closed meanwhile is
not moved back (`session_not_open`).

restore_files.description:
Whether to put files back as they were before the turn, from its
snapshots.

SessionUpdated.description: Session metadata changed: title, models, speed, level, queue length.

SessionUsage.description:
The live usage of a session: what `usage/get` returns and `usage.updated`
carries.

by_model.description: The same, per provider, model, role and speed.

cache_hit_rate.description: Cache reads as a share of all input tokens sent, from 0 to 1.

context.description:
What the context of the most recent request to the main model held,
by category: estimates, as the harness counts them. Added in step 24.

context_tokens.description: The tokens in the context of the most recent request to the main model.

limits.description: The latest limits each provider reported.

tokens_per_second.description: Output tokens per second of the most recent request.

totals.description:
Everything the session has used, out-of-band requests included
(compaction, titles).

anyOf.description: The provider's normal processing, at the model's normal prices. Every model has it, and it is what a request runs at when nothing else is asked for.
Faster output at a higher price, where the model offers it.
A value this version of the protocol does not know. Receivers need a default branch.

Speed.description: A speed tier, by name. Which ones a model offers is in its [`ModelInfo`](crate::model::ModelInfo).

SpeedCooldown.description:
Notice: a speed tier's cooldown began or ended. During a cooldown the
harness sends requests at `standard` and does not flip back and forth,
because each change of speed can cost a prompt-cache rewrite.

speed.description: The tier that is cooling down.

state.description: Whether the cooldown began or ended.

until.description: When it ends, for one that began.

anyOf.description: The model produces output tokens faster.
The request is served ahead of standard traffic: lower and steadier latency under load, the same generation speed.
The request is cheaper and may be slow, queued or turned away when the provider is busy.
A value this version of the protocol does not know. Receivers need a default branch.

SpeedEffect.description: What a speed tier buys, compared with `standard`.

SpeedFallback.description:
Notice: a request ran, or will run, at a different speed from the one the
session asked for. The usage record of the request says the same thing in
numbers: it is priced at the speed it ran at.

cooldown_until.description:
When the harness will ask for the requested speed again, if it has
put the tier in a cooldown.

message.description:
The notice in words, so that a client that does not know this kind of
notice can still show it.

requested.description: The speed the session asked for.

role.description: The role whose request it was.

served.description: The speed the request ran at, or will run at.

anyOf.description: The harness sent the request at another speed after the provider refused the one that was asked for.
The provider served the request at another speed and reported it.
A value this version of the protocol does not know. Receivers need a default branch.

SpeedFallbackBy.description: Who moved a request to another speed.

anyOf.description: The tier's own rate limit was reached.
The provider had no capacity for the tier.
The tier is in a cooldown after an earlier refusal.
The model in use does not offer the tier.
The provider reported another speed and gave no reason.

SpeedFallbackReason.description: Why a request did not run at the speed that was asked for.

SpeedOffer.description:
One speed tier a model offers besides `standard`, with everything that
makes it different from another provider's tier of the same name.

label.description: What the provider calls it, for display: "Fast mode", "Flex processing".

preview.description:
Whether the provider marks the tier as a preview that may change or
need access to be granted.

prices.description:
The tier's own full rate card. Absent when its price is not known, in
which case its usage shows tokens only.

separate_limit.description:
Whether the tier has a rate limit of its own, apart from the model's
standard limit.

shares_cache.description:
Whether a prompt-cache prefix written at `standard` can be read at
this tier and the other way round. `false` means a change of speed is
a cache miss. Absent when the provider does not say.

speed.description: The tier's name: what a setting names and what a usage record carries.

when_unavailable.description: What the provider does when it cannot serve the tier.

anyOf.description: It fails the request with a rate-limit or overload error. The harness decides whether to wait or to fall back.
It serves the request at `standard`, says so in the response, and bills it at the standard price.
A value this version of the protocol does not know. Receivers need a default branch.

SpeedUnavailable.description: What the provider does when it cannot serve a request at the tier that was asked for.

anyOf.description: The project's checks failed some rounds in a row.

rounds.description: The number of failed rounds in a row.

anyOf.description: An action outside the scope was needed.
Spending passed a threshold.
The time ran out.

anyOf.description: The model finished.
The model asked for tools to be run.
The response reached the output limit.
The request did not fit the context window.
The provider paused a server-side loop. The harness continues it.
The model declined.
A content filter stopped the response.
The model wrote a tool call that could not be read.
The request failed. The item's `error` says how.
The user or a signal interrupted the response. Set by the harness, never by a provider.

StopReason.description: Why a response from the model ended. Each provider's own value is mapped onto this set, and kept beside it as `raw_stop`.

StoredApproval.description: An approval the user gave earlier that still applies.

SummaryItem.description: A compaction summary. It starts a context epoch's history.

covers_through.description: The last item the summary covers.

usage.description: What the summarising request used and cost.

TargetDetail.description: The detail of an approval for access to a path or a host.

raw.description: The provider's own block, on assistant messages.

TimeTotals.description:
Where the wall time of some turns went, in milliseconds. Every moment of
a turn is in exactly one part, so the parts add up to `wall_ms`: a tool
that runs while the response is still arriving is in the model's time,
and a question to the user while a tool runs is in the tools'.

approval_ms.description:
Waiting for the user to answer whether a call may run, with no tool
running.

harness_ms.description: The harness's own work: assembling requests, recording, planning.

tools_ms.description: Waiting for tools once the response had ended.

wall_ms.description: Their wall time, from the prompt to `turn.completed`.

Timestamp.description:
A moment in time, in RFC 3339 form in UTC: `2026-11-12T10:15:02Z`.
Fractional seconds are allowed.

TokenUsage.description:
Token counts by class. The classes do not overlap: the tokens sent are
`input + cache_read + cache_write`.

cache_read.description: Input tokens read from the cache.

cache_write.description: Input tokens written to the cache, all lifetime classes together.

cache_write_classes.description: `cache_write` split by lifetime class, where the provider has classes.

input.description:
Input tokens billed at the normal rate: not read from the cache and
not written to it.

reasoning.description: The part of `output` that was reasoning, when the provider reports it.

ToolArgsDelta.description:
More of a tool call's arguments: a fragment of JSON text that is not
valid JSON until the call is complete.

ToolCallDelta.description: The model began a tool call.

ToolCallPart.description: A request by the model to run a tool.

arguments.description:
The arguments, as the JSON value the model wrote. When the model's
text was not valid JSON this is that text as a JSON string, and the
call's result is an error that says so.

id.description: The provider's id for the call. Its result names it.

raw.description:
The provider's own block. A protocol with a second id for the call
keeps it here.

ToolDetail.description: The detail of an approval for an extension or MCP tool.

arguments.description: The arguments the tool would be called with.

anyOf.description: The tool ran and succeeded.
The tool failed, or its arguments were invalid.
The call was not allowed to run.
The call was cancelled. The result holds the output so far.
A value this version of the protocol does not know. Receivers need a default branch.

ToolOutcome.description: How a tool call ended. Every started call ends with exactly one result.

ToolResultItem.description: The result of one tool call.

artifacts.description: Where the full output is, when the content was shortened.

content.description: What the model is shown, after the output policy.

payload.description:
A structured payload for front ends, whose shape belongs to the tool:
a diff, an exit status, match counts.

ToolResultPart.description: The result of one tool call, as the model sees it.

content.description: What the model is shown: text and images.

is_error.description:
Whether the call failed. A failure is a result, written so the model
can correct itself.

ToolTime.description: The time one tool took over some turns, in milliseconds.

approval_ms.description: How long its calls waited for the user's answer.

queued_ms.description:
How long its calls waited, once allowed, before they ran: for a slot,
for an earlier call they conflict with, or for the response to end.

running_ms.description:
Its calls' running time, added up. Calls that ran side by side are
each counted whole.

share_ms.description:
Its part of the turns' tool time (`TimeTotals::tools_ms`): when calls
run side by side each has an equal part of that moment.

TrustRequest.description: `trust/request`: may this project's executable resources be used?

resources.description: What it asks to be trusted with.

trusted.description:
The project is trusted already, and the question is about what is
new in it: its rules changed (each resource marked `changed`), or
git, now that it is a repository. `never` is not an answer to it;
`keep` is (since the follow-ups of step 23).

TrustResource.description: One thing a project asks to be trusted with.

changed.description: Whether it was trusted before and has changed since.

detail.description: What it would do, in full: the command, the rules.

anyOf.description: Permission rules that allow.
A hook.
An extension.
An MCP server.
Learned or shared commands used for the safe list.
Git reading the repository's own configuration, which can name programs for git to run (since step 23).
A setting of the project's that raises cost or widens access, held back until the project is trusted (since step 23).
A value this version of the protocol does not know. Receivers need a default branch.

TrustResourceKind.description: A kind of project resource that can run code or grant permissions.

keep.description:
With `trusted` false, to a question about a project trusted already
(the request's `trusted`): keep trusting it as it was, without what
is new, and remember that, so that what is new is not asked about
again while it stays as it is (since the follow-ups of step 23). An
answer with `keep` and `trusted` or `never`, `keep` to a project not
trusted, or `never` to one trusted, is refused (`invalid_answer`).

never.description:
With `trusted` false: remember the refusal, so that the project is
not asked about at later starts either (since step 23). It is kept
beside the trusted projects, and `cineris permissions trust` lifts it.
An answer with both `trusted` and `never` is refused
(`invalid_answer`), and the question stays open.

trusted.description: Whether the resources listed may be used.

anyOf.description: Nothing: the project is not trusted.
Trusted, its rules the ones the user saw.
Trusted, its rules changed since: what they could loosen is set aside until the change is approved.
The user said never to trust it: it is not asked about.
Trusted for now only, with nothing kept: for the run by the command line (`--trust-project`), or for the session by a yes the trust store could not keep (since the review of step 23).
A value this version of the protocol does not know. Receivers need a default branch.

TrustStanding.description: What the user has said of a project's trust (since step 23).

TurnCompleted.description:
The turn is over and nothing automatic remains: no retry pending, no
compaction running, no tool running. Clients wait on this one event.

error.description: The failure, when there was one.

usage.description: What the turn used and cost.

TurnId.description: One turn of a session: from a prompt until the session is settled again.

now.description:
Whether to stop running commands at once, without the polite
interrupt and the grace that normally come first: what a second
interrupt means. Absent or `false` is the ordinary interrupt, which
stays safe to send twice.

undelivered.description:
Steering prompts that had not been delivered, handed back so the
front end can put them in its editor. Queued prompts stay queued.

anyOf.description: The model ended normally.
It ended with an error.
The user or a signal interrupted it.
A configured limit stopped it.
A denied permission stopped it.
A value this version of the protocol does not know. Receivers need a default branch.

TurnOutcome.description: How a turn ended. It and a headless run's exit code always agree.

delivery.description:
How to deliver it if a turn is running. Required then, and ignored
when the session is idle.

TurnStartResult.description:
The result of `turn/start`. It means "accepted": the turn ends with the
`turn.completed` event, and the result never carries the model's answer.

turn_id.description:
The turn the prompt belongs to: the one it started, the running one
it steers, or the one it will start.

anyOf.description: By provider.
By model.
By project.
By the tool that recorded the usage.
By the speed the requests ran at.
A value this version of the protocol does not know. Receivers need a default branch.

UsageGroup.description: A way to group the rows of a usage report.

anyOf.description: The session named in the request.
The local calendar day.
The calendar week, or the last 7 days when configured as rolling.
The calendar month, or the last 30 days when configured as rolling.
Everything on record.
A value this version of the protocol does not know. Receivers need a default branch.

UsageRange.description: The period a usage report covers.

UsageRefreshParams.description:
`usage/refresh`: asks the documented usage endpoint of each provider the
user turned the refresh on for (`usage.refresh`), with that provider's
own credential. Only a `user` client may call it. Added in step 16.

providers.description:
Only these providers, each of which must be in `usage.refresh`.
Empty: every provider in it.

UsageRefreshResult.description: The result of `usage/refresh`: one entry for each provider asked.

providers.description: What each provider answered, in the order of `usage.refresh`.

UsageReport.description: Usage and cost over a range: the result of `usage/report`.

from.description: The start of the range. Absent for all time.

group_by.description: How the rows are grouped, outermost first.

limits.description: The latest limits each provider reported.

notes.description:
What to tell the person of the statistics behind the report, a
sentence each: a file set aside because it could not be read, one a
newer build wrote. Added in step 24.

recording.description:
Whether usage history is being recorded. When statistics are off,
only the session range has figures.

sources.description: The sources included: `cineris`, and other tools the user turned on.

time.description:
Where the time of the range's turns went, all rows together. Added
in step 16.

tools.description:
The time each tool took in the range, the most first. Added in step
16.

zone.description:
The time zone the days were counted in, as the user is shown it.
Added in step 16.

group_by.description: How to group the rows, outermost first. Empty: by provider, then model.

UsageRow.description:
One row of a usage report. The fields that are set are the ones the
report is grouped by.

project_label.description: The project's name or shortened path, for display.

source.description: The tool that recorded the usage: `cineris`, or another tool's id.

speed.description: The speed the requests ran at.

time.description:
Where the time of the turns in the row went: for a report grouped
by provider, model or project only, since a turn has no one speed
or source. Added in step 16.

UsageTotals.description: Usage added up over some requests: one row of a breakdown.

costs.description: The cost, one amount per basis. Empty when no price is known.

delivery.description: How it was delivered, when it was sent during a running turn.

parts.description: What the user sent: text and images.

anyOf.description: They passed.
A check failed in the turn and had not passed when the turn ended: at the round limit, after a round with nothing new, or a turn that then ended another way.
They did not run to a result: no files changed, no check is known, the mode is not `auto`, the project is not trusted, the level is `read-only`, or none had time or was allowed.
None failed, and some did not run to a result: blocked by the sandbox, stopped at their time limit, skipped or not allowed (since step 19).
A value this version of the protocol does not know. Receivers need a default branch.

Verification.description: What the project's checks said at the end of a turn.

VerificationNotice.description:
Notice: the project's checks, at the end of a turn that changed files
(`docs/architecture/15-efficiency.md`, "Automatic verification"; since
step 19).

round.description:
The round, counted from 1 in its turn. 0 in a notice that offers
the checks.

rounds.description: The most rounds the turn gets.

verdict.description: The turn's verdict so far, when a round ended.

anyOf.description: A round is starting: the checks it will run.
A round ended: how each check ended, and the verdict.
The checks did not run, and are offered: `verify.mode` is `ask`.
A value this version of the protocol does not know. Receivers need a default branch.

VerificationPhase.description: Which moment of verification a [`VerificationNotice`] tells of.
